items.excerpt: ## House GOP Blocks Impeachment Charges Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Nov 11, 2026 House Republicans on Tuesday blocked impeachment charges against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. By a margin of just seven votes, Republicans managed to bury the charges in committee through a 211-204 party-line procedural vote. Eleven Democrats skipped the vote, including Democratic Congressmember Nancy Pelosi of California. While House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is vying for the speakership in January, expressed support for Hegseth’s impeachment, many wondered how it was such a surprise that he was unable to corral Democratic votes to impeach Hegseth. President Trump hailed the outcome as an “exoneration.” Hours before the vote, Hegseth blasted the impeachment articles and said he’d carry out the same operations again. > Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth: “Let’s be clear about what this resolution actually does. It tells our enemies, Iran, the cartels, every adversary watching, that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations.” ## Sanders Says He Will Not Back Schumer for Senate Majority Leader Nov 11, 2026 Vermont’s independent Senator Bernie Sanders said Tuesday he will not back Senator Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader. Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan also said she won’t support Schumer until he presents a plan to govern differently. Senators-elect Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, Troy Jackson of Maine, Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, Juliana Stratton of Illinois and Adam Hamilton of Kansas have all said they won’t support Schumer, as has Senate candidate Scott Colom of Mississippi. This comes as Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland indicated Monday he’s open to running for Senate majority leader when the new Congress convenes in January. This is Senator Sanders. ... ## Rep. Jordan Elected as House GOP Leader as Senator Thune Reelected as Senate Republican Leader Nov 11, 2026 House Republicans elected Congressmember Jim Jordan, a staunch Trump ally, as their leader after last week’s sweeping midterm losses. Jordan will replace Speaker Mike Johnson come January when a new Democratic majority takes office with at least 256 seats in the House. In the Senate, Republicans reelected Senator John Thune of South Dakota as leader. Democrats currently have a 54-seat majority in the Senate, with the races in Alaska and Mississippi leaning toward Democrats. The Democratic Senate candidate in Mississippi, Scott Colom, leads his Republican opponent by 3,000 votes. ... ## Israeli Forces Kill at Least Eight Palestinians in Gaza Nov 11, 2026 In news from Gaza, Israeli forces have killed ⁠at least eight Palestinians, including a father and his 13-year-old son, in attacks on Gaza City and Khan Younis. Israel has conducted near-daily attacks on Gaza despite a so-called ceasefire brokered by the U.S., killing more than 1,600 Palestinians since the deal went into effect last October. This comes as damage and destruction caused by Israel’s relentless bombings on Gaza’s infrastructure since 2023 have contributed to worsening flash floods as the enclave faces another winter with torrential rains. Gaza’s stormwater and sewage networks are so deteriorated that thousands of tents are being flooded. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was not in attendance at the summit, where Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff renewed pressure to end the war. items.excerpt: ## Russia and Ukraine agree to a large prisoner exchange as talks conclude with no major breakthrough ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large prisoner exchange during U.S.-mediated talks. However, no major breakthroughs were announced in efforts to end the war that began nearly five years ago. The two-day session in Abu Dhabi was the first meeting in nine months. U.S. officials are determined to revive peace efforts, with envoys set to meet with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents. Fighting continues on the front line, with both countries using long-range missiles and drones. Ukrainian officials say three people were killed and 11 were injured after Russia launched a daytime attack on a market in the southern Odesa region. ## How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington WASHINGTON (AP) — Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, is under scrutiny after revelations of an affair with a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, who is suspected of spying. Nvidia produces crucial AI chips that both China and the U.S. covet, and the affair has sparked concerns about national security. The Department of Justice is probing whether a company tied to Alice Huang, Megaspeed, illegally funneled chips to China. Nvidia's board says there's “no reason to believe” secrets were compromised. President Donald Trump, a supporter of Jensen Huang, has downplayed the issue. And China has denied the allegations that Alice Huang was a spy. ... ## As higher prices seep into broader economy, Fed officials consider faster hikes WASHINGTON (AP) — More evidence this week of hot inflation in the U.S. was unpleasant news for the Federal Reserve, not to mention consumers: Rising prices may be spreading beyond the one-time shocks from tariffs and high gas prices into the wider economy, meaning that mortgages, credit cards and other forms of borrowing are likely to become increasingly expensive. Tuesday’s consumer price index report showed broadly rising costs across a range of goods and services. There is increasing anxiety among Fed officials that higher oil prices stemming from the Iran war may last longer than previously thought. ... ## Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak BUNIA, Congo (AP) — Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, highlighting the severity of the situation. The health ministry reported on Wednesday 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, making it Congo's deadliest outbreak. The crisis began in mid-May, and authorities have struggled to contain it due to armed conflicts, a health system crisis, poor roads, and violence fueled by mistrust. The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to eight provinces. Health workers face attacks, and experts urge more efforts to contain the disease, which has spread to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. ## World leaders urge stronger and faster action at UN climate talks over inadequate response ANTALYA, Turkey (AP) — World leaders were urged to act decisively to curb global warming as formal talkes opened Wednesday at the United Nations climate conference in Turkey. The summit comes after a year of deadly floods, heat waves and other climate-related disasters. “We know the truth. Now we must act on it,” U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres told the COP31 gathering. What will be accomplished remains uncertain as laders of some of the world’s biggest polluting nations — including the United States, China and India — skipped the summit. A new report warns of a widening gap between countries’ climate pledges and emissions cuts.

items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The core index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent underlying inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy. A few hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he planned to support a quarter-point increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting unless core CPI came in at 0.3% or more. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said at a conference in London hosted by King's Business School and the Money Macro and Finance Society. Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risked hurting the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation was too high and appeared to be broadening. items.title: Inflation runs hotter than expected as higher prices extend beyond the gas station
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON – U.S. inflation was higher than expected last month as the rising prices that powered sweeping Democratic victories in last week’s midterm elections appear likely to pose ongoing challenges for the White House and the Federal Reserve. The consumer price index rose 0.4% from September to October, the Labor Department said Tuesday, down from 0.6% the previous month. The government did not report a yearly inflation rate because last year’s government shutdown meant no data was released for October 2025. But excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 0.3%, the same as the preceding month. Both figures were a tenth of a point higher than forecast, and at an annual rate would be well above the Fed’s 2% target. The new inflation data heightened concerns that strong consumer and business spending, combined with higher gas prices and supply disruptions stemming from tariffs and global turmoil, are creating increasingly stubborn inflation that could extend beyond temporary spikes in prices at the gas pump. The economy expanded at a 3.4% annual rate in the July-September quarter, mostly driven by consumer spending. “It’s worrisome. There is a sense that inflation is broad, persistent, a little bit everywhere,” said Riccardo Trezzi, founder of Underlying Inflation, a consulting firm, and a former Fed economist. “The Fed should be very worried.” Using rough estimates for last October’s data, Trezzi calculates that consumer prices rose 4% in October from a year ago, up from 3.7% in September. Core prices rose 2.8%, he estimates, up from 2.6%. ... Higher gas prices may have begun to spread through economy Gas prices rose 1% from September to October, the government said, a stiff increase but still much lower than in previous months. Gas prices have soared more than 37% from a year ago. Still, oil prices have fallen sharply in recent days on hopes that the Iran conflict is fading, and gas costs have declined this month. Yet there are signs higher energy prices are spreading into other parts of the economy, with airfares, public transportation, and delivery services all jumping in price. Electricity prices rose 0.9% from September to October, the most since April, and grocery prices jumped 0.4%, a painful rise after years of increases. Beef prices rose 0.9% last month, after jumping nearly 14% in the first half of this year. Restaurant prices rose 0.5% from September to October, the most since January 2024. Rising shipping prices, driven up by more expensive gas, have lifted costs for restaurants and grocery stores, which may be passing them on to consumers. Inflation has also been worsened by the massive investments flowing into artificial intelligence, which has contributed to higher prices for computer chips, electricity and consumer electronics. Voters swept dozens of candidates into office who had pledged to slow data center construction. Computer prices jumped 0.5% last month, the government report showed, after rising nearly 10% in the year ending in September, lifted by more expensive chips. The cost of computers had been retreating for years as semiconductor chips became more efficient. That trend reversed course this year as prices rose sharply. ... Outside of inflation, other measures show the economy is largely doing well. The unemployment rate is a low 4.1% and growth is steady.

The cases have sparked a wider reckoning about celebrity misconduct in the U.K. Walliams, a feted children's author and well-known TV personality, is facing allegations of using his fame to exploit young female fans. He had sought to block news organizations from publishing these claims, but a judge dismissed his bid. Walliams has not been charged, but the revelations have prompted questions about the media and entertainment industries' roles in enabling such behavior. Authorities are now urging stronger protections for women.

items.excerpt: La Bola Negra breaks a UK record: Altitude’s La Bola Negra, which won the London Film Festival’s Audience Award, has had the biggest opening ever for a Spanish-language film at the UK-Ireland box office, according to Screen Daily. It took £536,000 including previews, ahead of the £433,000 of Pedro Almodóvar’s Volver in 2006, with £354,000 from 130 cinemas at the weekend, a strong £2,723 average. Volver remains the highest-grossing Spanish-language film in the territory, with £2.8 million, and La Bola Negra has a chance of passing it over its run. It follows a record-breaking start for the film in Spain, where it’s Spain’s highest-grossing local film of the year, with $43 million worldwide, and it’s Spain’s Oscar entry. ...
